findings.title: The client-side upload limit ignores configured size settings
findings.body: This hard-codes every upload type to 10 MB instead of using the configured per-type limit. Sites that allow attachments larger than 10 MB will now reject them in the browser before the server can accept them; the same applies to images when the configured limit is higher. Keep the client limit aligned with the applicable setting, or make this a deliberate independent limit that is configurable.

findings.title: Oversized animated GIFs can be flattened during upload
findings.body: This passes `allow_animated_thumbnails` as the switch for the GIF downsize implementation. When that setting is false, `OptimizedImage.downsize_instructions` uses ImageMagick with `#{from}[0]`, which processes only the first frame; the resulting file replaces the uploaded source, permanently discarding the GIF animation. The thumbnail setting should not determine whether the original upload's animation is preserved.
